scope: These results apply to the maintained kit fixtures and the component gallery in headless Chromium on macOS. 1.3.0 adds measured period sizes for the tree, up-down control, slider thumb, browser-drawn list box and toolbar, a property sheet layout, a wizard button row, a default-button frame that follows the focus in dialogs, and tab arrow keys that stop at the ends. These are covered by tests and by the example audit but have not been judged in use by a person. The generated Electron editor was not built, packaged or launched. Consumer applications, native window behavior on any operating system, OS display scaling and screen readers require their own checks.

windows_95_comparison.reference: Windows 95 4.00.1111 C (OSR2.5) installed from the owner's media in QEMU, captured 19 November 2026 at 24-bit, 16-bit and 256 colours by tools/win95-reference
windows_95_comparison.result: At 24-bit, of 54 paired control states: 21 match pixel for pixel, 17 have the same edges at a different size, 6 differ in size and were not compared pixel by pixel, 10 differ in drawing.
windows_95_comparison.scope: The 54-state result above is the 1.2.0 comparison with the comfortable atlas and was not re-run for 1.3.0. user, gdi and their 32-bit counterparts report version 4.0.0.950, as in the 1995 release; comctl32 is 4.70 (1996), so status bar, tab, slider and progress results describe that library. The original August 1995 release was not captured. Captures are not distributed.
windows_95_comparison.example_audit: For 1.3.0 each of the 38 widget examples was compared, in the period density, with captures and step-by-step recordings of the same system (docs/example-audit.md): 27 examples verified (11 of them apart from recorded browser limits), 2 verified with open differences (check box and option button rows 1 or 2 px further apart), 3 partly checked and 6 not verifiable. Verified means every difference found was fixed or recorded with a reason, not that the example is identical.
